events.title: The recession reaches its low point
events.description: US economic activity reaches the turning point later identified by the NBER. That official announcement comes in July 1983.

events.title: A new missile-defense proposal
events.description: President Reagan announces a research effort to defend against nuclear missiles. It becomes a major Cold War debate.

events.title: Challenger is lost
events.description: Seven people die when the space shuttle breaks apart after launch. NASA pauses shuttle flights and investigates.

what_happened_next.text: The economy began growing again, but you could not have known the turning point on decision day. Over this five-year window, all seven choices gained value. Apple finished ahead of the other six, while the international share basket also rose strongly. The route was not smooth, and choosing a different endpoint could change the ranking.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: Recession, international debt and computer-company competition made the outlook uncertain.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: Each holding compounded along its own path. Broad share baskets spread company-specific risk, but they still moved sharply. Interest paid by cash and bonds also added up over five years.
reflection.what_faded_away: A musical opening and a headline about stolen computer designs were memorable news. Neither told you the five-year ranking of these investments.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: No one could know the exact size or order of the gains in these seven choices. A gloomy starting point did not guarantee a poor five-year result.
